findings.title: record() write-error accounting path (get_error -> _events decrement) is never exercised
findings.evidence:
if _file.get_error() != OK:
		# The line did not reach disk — drop it from the count so the chip
		# never overstates what persisted (disk full, ejected media, ...).
		_events -= 1
		push_warning("playtest: write to %s failed (error %d) — event dropped" % [path, _file.get_error()])
findings.detail: Open-failure and collision guards are covered, but this mid-write branch and its _events decrement never run in any test — a blind-spot the brief names explicitly.
findings.recommended_fix: Inject a failing FileAccess after begin() (fill/readonly path) and assert event_count() excludes the dropped line and the warning fires.

findings.title: age_picked and street_name hooks are never exercised — the scene test emits the signals directly, skipping the record handlers
findings.evidence:
func _on_age_picked(bracket: String) -> void:
	_record("age_picked", {"bracket": bracket})
	_close_popup()
	_age_picked.emit(bracket)
---
accept.pressed.connect(func() -> void:
	_record("street_name", {"name": current["name"]})
	_street_name_picked.emit(current["name"])
)
--- test:
		_street._age_picked.emit("8-10")
		_street._street_name_picked.emit("Fresh Lane")
findings.detail: Both handlers record-then-emit; the test emits the signals directly, skipping the handlers, so age_picked and street_name are absent from the log, not merely unasserted.
findings.recommended_fix: Press the real age ACCEPT and street-name ACCEPT buttons via their pressed signal (or call _on_age_picked) so the record handlers run; assert events.has('age_picked') / events.has('street_name').

findings.title: Collision guard compounds suffixes (X-2-3.jsonl) instead of incrementing (X-3.jsonl)
findings.evidence:
var target := path
	var n := 2
	while FileAccess.file_exists(target):
		target = "%s-%d.%s" % [target.get_basename(), n, target.get_extension()]
		n += 1
findings.detail: The loop rebases off `target`, which mutates each pass, so a 3rd same-second session becomes session-X-2-3.jsonl, not session-X-3.jsonl; the docstring promises a '-2/-3 suffix'.
findings.recommended_fix: Rebase off the original path in the loop: use path.get_basename()/path.get_extension() instead of the mutating target.

findings.title: Scorecard 'First wage <60s' formula uses session-wide elapsed_ms; wrong after NEW GAME
findings.evidence:
| First wage <60s | first `first_wage` after the latest `boot`: `elapsed_ms` ÷ 1000 = ____ s | PASS / FAIL |
---
	_start_ms = Time.get_ticks_msec()
		"elapsed_ms": Time.get_ticks_msec() - _start_ms,
findings.detail: _start_ms is set once in begin() and never reset on boot, so for a NEW GAME segment Row 1's elapsed_ms ÷ 1000 yields total session time (minutes), not that segment's first-wage time. Row 2 (FIND WORK) already subtracts its boot's elapsed_ms.
findings.recommended_fix: Tell the observer to subtract the segment boot's elapsed_ms (as Row 2 implies), or log a per-segment elapsed reset on each boot.

findings.evidence:
Story table row: "| `game/scenes/street.tscn` | EDIT | `PlaytestChip` Label under `Root/HUD` (after DebugButton), `unique_name_in_owner`, `visible = false`, font_size 20, soft ink |"
street.tscn:159: "[node name="PlaytestChip" type="Label" parent="."]"
Same story file, Completion Notes: "`PlaytestChip` pinned top-left OUTSIDE the centered HUD row"

AC5 is still met (chip is gated on debug+flag), but the planning table contradicts both the code and the file's own completion notes — a stale artifact left when the chip was moved during the review round.

findings.title: --playtest-log override accepted unsanitized; no user:// confinement or traversal filter
findings.detail: Override value is returned verbatim and reaches make_dir_recursive_absolute + truncate WRITE with no user:// confinement or '..' filter. Safe today only because the source is OS.get_cmdline_user_args() (trusted launcher); no untrusted boundary is crossed.
findings.recommended_fix: If the arg source ever becomes less-trusted (config file, remote), confine to user:// and reject '..'/absolute paths. Meanwhile, state the launcher-trust assumption in the override docstring so future wiring doesn't silently widen exposure.

findings.title: _do_repair re-fetches the asset via find_asset when repair_asset already returns it
findings.detail: repair_asset already returns the repaired asset in result["asset"], identical to upgrade_asset. The added find_asset call re-queries state unnecessarily and diverges from the sibling pattern ten lines above.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the find_asset line; use the returned asset: var asset: Dictionary = result["asset"], then _record("repair", {"name": asset["name"]}).
